nina: quick question about safetensors migration: can we add a lightweight manifest diff header so runtime can decide patch vs full reload?

alex: what fields in header? size checksum? quant flags?

peter: propose header fields: format_version, quant_type, checksum_root, segment_count, supports_atomic_swap boolean. if checksum_root matches existing, we can do a cheap header-only swap.

nina: nice. how to handle partial mismatch in segments? maybe include per-segment checksums so runtime can only fetch changed segments. reduces network IO.

alex: that complicates uploader but huge win for large models. add segment-level byte ranges and checksum in manifest. runtime can request changed ranges via ranged GETs.

loader-bot: note: we already support ranged reads in the CDN layer but need to ensure signed URL expiration supports longer ranged fetches for large segments.

peter: also add a small TTL hint in header to suggest warm priority; e.g., header.warm_hint = "hot"/"cool"/"cold". uploader can mark curated models as hot which prober prioritizes.

nina: ops: need metrics for header-swap-success, segment_delta_bytes, ranged_fetch_latency.

alex: implementation plan: week1 manifest schema extension + uploader changes, week2 runtime patching logic + unit tests, week3 canary.

peter: add fallback: if ranged fetch fails repeatedly -> fall back to full shard stream to be robust.

nina: action items:
- nina: schema PR + examples (Mon)
- alex: runtime ranged-merge prototype (Wed)
- peter: prober prioritization update (Fri)
